refiling-er27-454-pjm-backstop.point: The refiling matches the October 29 filing in ER27-330 and changes only its metadata code from compliance to section 205.
refiling-er27-454-pjm-backstop.quote: substantively identical to the October 29, 2026 filing submitted in Docket No. ER27-330-000

refiling-er27-454-pjm-backstop.point: PJM asks for a February 28, 2027 effective date, one record on January 29, 2027, and an order by January 29, 2027.
refiling-er27-454-pjm-backstop.quote: PJM is also requesting that the Commission issue an order on all aspects of this filing no later than January 29, 2027

refiling-er27-454-pjm-backstop.point: PJM seeks conditional waiver of shortage investigation and backstop declaration rules if the 2029/2030 auction clears short.
refiling-er27-454-pjm-backstop.quote: conditionally requests waiver of the requirement in Tariff, Attachment DD, section 16.2

refiling-er27-454-pjm-backstop.point: Electric Distributors will report incremental Large Load growth from the 2026 peak to the 2028/2029 expected peak, replacing the Load Adjustment proxy.
refiling-er27-454-pjm-backstop.quote: rather than relying on Load Adjustment data as a proxy for Large Load growth, PJM is proposing to require Electric Distributors

refiling-er27-454-pjm-backstop.point: PJM allocates the Initial RBP Target by zone share of incremental Large Load growth, net of bilateral offsets, fixed for the 15-year commitment.
refiling-er27-454-pjm-backstop.quote: That allocation to the zone/area will remain fixed throughout the 15-year RBP commitment period.

refiling-er27-454-pjm-backstop.point: PJM cuts the RBP Credit Rate from $1.5 million per MW to 40 percent of net present value, about $686,000 per MW at the cap.
refiling-er27-454-pjm-backstop.quote: the proposed methodology produces an illustrative RBP Credit Rate of approximately $686,000 per MW.

refiling-er27-454-pjm-backstop.point: PJM lengthens LSE collateral notice to at least 75 days and broadens acceptable collateral forms.
refiling-er27-454-pjm-backstop.quote: PJM is proposing that LSEs be provided at least 75 days

refiling-er27-454-pjm-backstop.point: An LSE that withdraws from PJM stays responsible for its remaining RBP Charges, rather than the exiting Transmission Owner.
refiling-er27-454-pjm-backstop.quote: such Load Serving Entity shall be responsible for the remainder of the RBP Charges allocated to it

notice-cnf-20261102.point: The notice lists ER27-330-000, PJM's proposed Reliability Backstop Procurement amendments in ER26-3380, filed October 29, 2026.
notice-cnf-20261102.quote: Proposed Amendments to the Reliability Backstop Procurement in ER26-3380 to be effective 1/15/2027.

notice-cnf-20261102.point: The errata filing ER27-330-001 was filed October 30, 2026 and carries the same November 30 comment date.
notice-cnf-20261102.quote: Errata to Correct Metadata and Waiver Request in RBP Compliance Filing to be effective 1/29/2027.

errata-er27-330-pjm-backstop.point: PJM entered January 15, 2027 instead of January 29, 2027 as the effective date for section 18.3A in the metadata.
errata-er27-330-pjm-backstop.quote: PJM incorrectly entered an effective date of January 15, 2027, instead of January 29, 2027.

errata-er27-330-pjm-backstop.point: The October 29 filing sought effective dates of January 29, 2027 for section 18.3A and February 28, 2027 for the rest.
errata-er27-330-pjm-backstop.quote: proposed new Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.3A become effective January 29, 2027, and the remainder of the proposed Tariff revisions become effective February 28, 2027.

errata-er27-330-pjm-backstop.point: PJM's one-time waiver request covers sections 16.2 and 16.3, and applies if the 2029/2030 Base Residual Auction clears short.
errata-er27-330-pjm-backstop.quote: PJM seeks a one-time waiver of Tariff, Attachment DD, sections 16.2 and 16.3 upon completion of the 2029/2030 Base Residual Auction in the event such auction clears short.

filing-er27-330-pjm-rbp-amendments.point: The filing proposes new rules on who pays RBP Charges, LSE credit, and notice to exiting LSEs.
filing-er27-330-pjm-rbp-amendments.quote: this filing proposes modifications to establish just and reasonable rules to (i) allocate responsibility for RBP Charges to certain Load Serving Entities (“LSE”); (ii) require LSEs responsible for RBP Charges to post an appropriate level of credit;

filing-er27-330-pjm-rbp-amendments.point: PJM asks for February 28, 2027 effectiveness for most revisions and an order by January 29, 2027.
filing-er27-330-pjm-rbp-amendments.quote: PJM is also requesting that the Commission issue an order on all aspects of this filing no later than January 29, 2027

filing-er27-330-pjm-rbp-amendments.point: PJM requests a 32-day comment period ending November 30, 2026.
filing-er27-330-pjm-rbp-amendments.quote: PJM moves for the Commission to establish an extended, 32-day comment period, such that comments and interventions would be due November 30, 2026.

filing-er27-330-pjm-rbp-amendments.point: Electric Distributors would report aggregate incremental Large Load peak growth in place of Load Adjustment data as the allocation basis.
filing-er27-330-pjm-rbp-amendments.quote: rather than relying on Load Adjustment data as a proxy for Large Load growth, PJM is proposing to require Electric Distributors outside of a Fixed Resource Requirement (“FRR”) Service Area to report, by no later than seven days prior to the commencement of the RBP, the aggregate incremental peak Large Load growth between the 2026 actual summer peak and the 2028/2029 Delivery Year expected summer peak

filing-er27-330-pjm-rbp-amendments.point: PJM cuts the LSE credit rate to 40% of net present value, about $686,000 per MW at most, from $1.5 million per MW.
filing-er27-330-pjm-rbp-amendments.quote: PJM proposes to set the RBP Credit Rate at 40% of the net present value of the total RBP payment obligation.

filing-er27-330-pjm-rbp-amendments.point: PJM lengthens the notice before LSE collateral is due, from 15 days to at least 75 days.
filing-er27-330-pjm-rbp-amendments.quote: PJM is proposing that LSEs be provided at least 75 days’ notice of their collateral obligation prior to a given Delivery Year before the LSE must have the requisite RBP Collateral posted.

filing-er27-330-pjm-rbp-amendments.point: PJM adds surety bonds to the accepted forms of RBP collateral.
filing-er27-330-pjm-rbp-amendments.quote: PJM is proposing to revise the definition of RBP Collateral to include surety bonds,

filing-er27-330-pjm-rbp-amendments.point: On Transmission Owner exit, PJM would charge the exiting LSEs for their allocated RBP Charges.
filing-er27-330-pjm-rbp-amendments.quote: PJM proposes to require that LSEs, rather than exiting Transmission Owners, cover costs commensurate with the RBP Charges allocated to them.

filing-er27-330-pjm-rbp-amendments.point: PJM keeps the 2028/2029 auction shortfall as the Initial RBP Target basis and updates load and resource inputs.
filing-er27-330-pjm-rbp-amendments.quote: PJM proposes to retain the 2028/2029 Delivery Year as the basis for the Initial RBP Target while updating the

filing-er27-330-pjm-rbp-amendments.point: PJM seeks a one-time waiver of the shortage investigation requirement if the 2029/2030 auction clears short, and expects to start the RBP March 1, 2027.
filing-er27-330-pjm-rbp-amendments.quote: PJM seeks a one-time waiver of Tariff, Attachment DD, section 16.2 upon completion of the 2029/2030 Base Residual Auction in the event such auction clears short.

notice-er26-3380-abeyance.point: Initial briefs in EL26-108 move from November 13, 2026 to January 11, 2027 and reply briefs from December 3, 2026 to January 26, 2027.
notice-er26-3380-abeyance.quote: the deadline for submission of initial briefs in Docket No. EL26-108-000 is extended from November 13, 2026 to 5pm on January 11, 2027, and the deadline for reply briefs is extended from December 3, 2026 to 5pm on January 26, 2027.

notice-er26-3380-answer-period.point: Answers to PJM's abeyance motion are due by 5:00 pm Eastern on October 21, 2026.
notice-er26-3380-answer-period.quote: answers to PJM’s motion are due by 5:00 pm Eastern Time on October 21, 2026.

motion-er26-3380-pjm-abeyance.point: PJM requests abeyance of the paper hearing pending a new section 205 filing responding to the September 29 Order.
motion-er26-3380-pjm-abeyance.quote: hold the paper hearing proceedings, including any additional briefings, in this docket in abeyance pending resolution of PJM’s forthcoming filing

motion-er26-3380-pjm-abeyance.point: The September 29 Order accepted the backstop rules but suspended them five months to review cost allocation, Transmission Owner exit rules and LSE collateral.
motion-er26-3380-pjm-abeyance.quote: suspended those rules for five months to allow time for further briefing through a paper hearing process to further review three discrete areas of the RBP: cost allocation, Transmission Owner exit rules, and LSE collateral requirements.

motion-er26-3380-pjm-abeyance.point: PJM plans to file the new section 205 proposal by October 29, 2026.
motion-er26-3380-pjm-abeyance.quote: a new FPA section 205 filing that addresses, inter alia, cost allocation issues, Transmission Owner exit responsibilities, and LSE collateral requirements as they relate to RBP by October 29, 2026.

statement-er26-3380-doe.point: DOE ties its position to the Ratepayer Protection Pledge, under which large loads fund the generation and infrastructure they require.
statement-er26-3380-doe.quote: large electric energy loads—not American households or other business ratepayers—must fund the electric energy generation and related infrastructure that such new large load projects require.

statement-er26-3380-doe.point: PJM missed its reliability requirement by 6,623 MW in the 2027/28 auction and 6,831 MW in the 2028/29 auction.
statement-er26-3380-doe.quote: PJM then fell 6,831 MW short for its 2028/29 delivery year auction in July 2026.

statement-er26-3380-doe.point: DOE commends FERC's separate proceeding requiring the six RTOs and ISOs to justify or reform large load interconnection rules.
statement-er26-3380-doe.quote: to require the six regional transmission organizations or independent system operators under its jurisdiction to justify or reform their rules governing how data centers, manufacturing facilities, and other large energy users connect to the electric grid.

statement-er26-3380-doe.point: PJM's two-year lookback may not allocate capacity costs to all large loads that caused the shortfall.
statement-er26-3380-doe.quote: PJM’s cost allocation methodology (looking back only two years) does not appear to sufficiently allocate the costs of new capacity to serve all large loads that have caused the current resource adequacy shortfall.

statement-er26-3380-doe.point: PJM needs project-level large load identification to track whether projects enter service, are delayed or cancelled.
statement-er26-3380-doe.quote: PJM should have sufficient data to accurately identify the material large load projects reflected in its forecasts and monitor their development.

statement-er26-3380-doe.point: DOE supports crediting new capacity against the backstop target and asks PJM to create a clear path for build, bring or buy options.
statement-er26-3380-doe.quote: PJM’s current RBP process does not establish a clear path for such optionality and should be revised to do so.

filing-20260928-4001.point: Pallone urges FERC to approve PJM's two proposals in part, with exceptions.
filing-20260928-4001.quote: I urge FERC to approve them in part, with a few important exceptions.

filing-20260928-4001.point: He supports requiring data centers to bring new generation and excluding those that refuse from the capacity auction.
filing-20260928-4001.quote: it must retain a critical provision to exclude any future data center load that refuses to procure its own generation capacity from PJM's capacity auction.

filing-20260928-4001.point: He says the backstop covers only the roughly 6.8 GW gap and wants all data center capacity costs allocated to the zones driving growth.
filing-20260928-4001.quote: The RBP only covers the approximately 6.8 gigawatt gap between PJM's reliability targets and recent generation capacity

filing-20260928-4001.point: He asks FERC to reject the provision that ends the bring-your-own-capacity requirement after three years of meeting the reliability requirement.
filing-20260928-4001.quote: letting new data centers off the hook after three years without a crisis does not meet the moment.

filing-20260928-4001.point: He wants PJM's large load registry to be public as far as possible.
filing-20260928-4001.quote: that registry – or as much of it as possible – must be public.

filing-20260928-4001.point: He asks FERC to ensure state regulators get the information needed to allocate data center costs, and to act quickly on the show cause orders.
filing-20260928-4001.quote: to act expeditiously in its related show-cause orders for grid operators around the country.

filing-20260925-5208.point: The Market Monitor says the shortfall comes entirely from data center load and PJM's approach keeps imposing those costs on other customers.
filing-20260925-5208.quote: The shortfall identified in the RBP Filing is a result solely of data center demand.

filing-20260925-5208.point: It cites $29.4 billion of capacity market costs and 20,539.7 MW of data center load left in the 2029/2030 auction.
filing-20260925-5208.quote: add to the $29.4 billion of capacity market costs that have resulted from the inclusion of data centers

filing-20260925-5208.point: PJM pushes allocation to states and distribution companies instead of assigning data center costs to data centers.
filing-20260925-5208.quote: PJM is attempting to evade its responsibility to directly ensure that data centers pay their own costs by shifting that responsibility to the states and the EDCs.

filing-20260925-5208.point: The Monitor recommends rejection and a two-week Section 206 directive, including removing unbuilt data center load from auctions.
filing-20260925-5208.quote: The Market Monitor continues to recommend that the Commission reject the RBP Filing and direct PJM, under the Commission’s FPA Section 206 authority, to file, within two weeks, a solution

filing-20260925-5208.point: New data center loads would need 15-year bilateral contracts with new generation that allow no cost or risk shifting.
filing-20260925-5208.quote: PJM should establish criteria to be included in the RAA defining the obligations of LSEs to require that new data center loads have 15 year bilateral contracts with new generation

filing-20260925-5208.point: The Monitor says the backstop and the interim service use inconsistent definitions of qualifying capacity, with bilateral terms as short as five years.
filing-20260925-5208.quote: The RBP Filing includes inconsistent definitions of capacity that will result in unintended consequences for reliability and capacity market prices in the future.

filing-20260910-5296.point: PJM says no protest undermines its one-time backstop procurement as just and reasonable.
filing-20260910-5296.quote: PJM’s RBP proposal is a just and reasonable and not unduly discriminatory or preferential means to procure capacity through a one-time backstop procurement.

filing-20260910-5296.point: PJM says it frames the RBP around the region's 67 million people in 13 states and the District of Columbia.
filing-20260910-5296.quote: to keep the lights on for 67 million people across 13 states and the District of Columbia

filing-20260910-5296.point: PJM is open to specific adjustments in a compliance filing if FERC orders them.
filing-20260910-5296.quote: adjustments to incorporate intervenors’ suggestions into the RBP proposal in a compliance filing if so ordered by the Commission.

filing-20260910-5296.point: PJM says Electric Distributors only report and administer, and do not bear RBP Charges unless they are also the LSE.
filing-20260910-5296.quote: Electric Distributors perform a reporting or administrative role in the RBP

filing-20260910-5296.point: PJM ties the 15-Delivery Year maximum term to the NEDC and governors' principles.
filing-20260910-5296.quote: the fixed, maximum 15-Delivery Year term is informed by the NEDC/PJM Governors’ Principles

filing-20260910-5296.point: PJM defends the $555/MW-day UCAP cap as a MW-weighted average on a pay-as-bid procurement.
filing-20260910-5296.quote: PJM has proposed that the levelized procurement cost of all selected RBP Sell Offers not exceed a maximum willingness to pay of $555/MW-day UCAP, on a MW-weighted average basis over all Delivery Years of the RBP.

filing-20260910-5296.point: PJM defends sizing the cost allocation on a snapshot of the 2028/2029 shortfall.
filing-20260910-5296.quote: The Commission has long held that relying on snapshots is an acceptable and appropriate method for establishing baselines or targets,

filing-20260910-5296.point: PJM defends the LSE collateral requirement as protecting other ratepayers.
filing-20260910-5296.quote: the basic need for a collateral requirement should not be controversial.

filing-20260910-5296.point: PJM says its Transmission Owner exit terms give enough notice.
filing-20260910-5296.quote: None of these arguments render PJM’s proposed Tariff revisions unjust and unreasonable.

filing-20260821-5306.point: The Coalition supports the backstop as a one-time measure and wants bilateral procurement kept as the preferred path.
filing-20260821-5306.quote: DCC supports moving forward with the RBP as a limited, one-time backstop.

filing-20260821-5306.point: PJM should not procure duplicative capacity for a customer that has arranged qualifying new capacity.
filing-20260821-5306.quote: Where a customer has arranged for qualifying new capacity to serve its incremental demand, PJM should not procure duplicative capacity on that customer’s behalf.

filing-20260821-5306.point: PJM proposes about 6.8 GW of new capacity under commitments of up to fifteen years.
filing-20260821-5306.quote: PJM proposes to procure approximately 6.8 GW of new capacity through commitments that may extend for as long as fifteen years.

filing-20260821-5306.point: Costs of serving new large loads should fall on the new large loads, not existing customers.
filing-20260821-5306.quote: should be borne by new large loads contributing to resource inadequacy and should not be shifted to existing residential, commercial, or industrial customers

filing-20260821-5306.point: DCC and the Virginia State Corporation Commission agreed to develop model retail tariff provisions for backstop costs.
filing-20260821-5306.quote: DCC and the Virginia State Corporation Commission have agreed to work together to develop model retail tariff provisions designed to appropriately assign RBP costs

filing-20260821-5306.point: Success is measured by megawatts reaching commercial operation, which depends on interconnection and transmission upgrades.
filing-20260821-5306.quote: measure of success should not be how many MW PJM contracts for, but how many MW actually reach commercial operation in time to address the identified reliability need.

filing-20260821-5183.point: The advocates say RBP cost allocation to large loads depends on state action, and where states do not act, zonal charges fall on the general ratepayer body.
filing-20260821-5183.quote: where a state does not act—or acts late—zonal RBP charges are allocated onto the general ratepayer body within the

filing-20260821-5183.point: They say RBP's design contradicts its stated 6.8 GW reliability need through opt-outs, 15-year terms and no market mitigation.
filing-20260821-5183.quote: PJM says that reliability demands that nearly 7 gigawatts of new supply be procured in the near-term, yet permits an untold number of megawatts (or possibly gigawatts) to opt-out of the auction

filing-20260821-5183.point: They say the $555/MW-day price ceiling comes from a one-year capacity design and does not fit a commitment of up to 15 years.
filing-20260821-5183.quote: A cap set on that basis is irrelevant to the determination of what should be paid

filing-20260821-5183.point: They put 15 years of RBP charges on a 6,831 MW total at about $20.8 billion.
filing-20260821-5183.quote: $555/MW-day x 365 days x 15 years would be $20,756,847,375.

filing-20260821-5183.point: Option One: refile as a subscription model in which load-serving entities set the procurement quantity and bear credit obligations.
filing-20260821-5183.quote: PJM should be directed to refile the RBP as a "subscription" model

filing-20260821-5183.point: Option Two: advance IRAS so large loads from 2028/2029 either bring their own resources or are treated as first-off in emergencies.
filing-20260821-5183.quote: the Commission should, in lieu of approving the RBP, advance the effective date of IRAS

filing-20260821-5183.point: As a fallback, they ask that any approval limit the procurement period to five years.
filing-20260821-5183.quote: The Commission should limit the RBP procurement period to five years

filing-20260821-5317.point: The Market Monitor says the RBP filing is unsupported and should be rejected.
filing-20260821-5317.quote: The RBP Filing has not been supported as just and reasonable, and it should be rejected.

filing-20260821-5317.point: It asks FERC to find current PJM rules for serving data centers unjust and unreasonable under FPA section 206.
filing-20260821-5317.quote: an order should issue, finding that the existing rules relating to resource adequacy for serving data centers in the PJM Region are unjust and unreasonable under Section 206 of the Federal Power Act.

filing-20260821-5317.point: Proposed remedy: new data center load has 15-year bilateral contracts with new generation, with no cost or risk shifted to other customers.
filing-20260821-5317.quote: new data center loads have 15 year bilateral contracts with new generation that do not permit any cost or risk shifting to other customers.

filing-20260821-5317.point: It attributes $29.4 billion of added capacity cost to data center load.
filing-20260821-5317.quote: The addition of data center load has resulted in adding $29.4 billion to the cost of capacity, higher energy costs, higher transmission costs, and a significant degradation of system reliability.

filing-20260821-5317.point: It argues the RBP assigns data center costs and risks to other customers, contrary to the Ratepayer Protection Pledge and Principles.
filing-20260821-5317.quote: PJM’s proposed RBP auction defines a shortfall that is based entirely on data center load yet assigns the costs and risks associated with meeting that shortfall to other PJM customers.

filing-20260821-5317.point: It says the RBP turns the must buy/must sell capacity market into must buy/option to sell at the highest price.
filing-20260821-5317.quote: The PJM RBP Filing would replace the must buy/must sell design with a must buy/option to sell at the highest price design.

filing-20260821-5317.point: Its attached design would include all data centers of 5.0 MW or more and sell only 15-year capacity from new generation.
filing-20260821-5317.quote: All data centers with expected demand greater than or equal to 5.0 MW would be included in the auction.

filing-20260821-5281.point: OCC says the backstop shifts the cost and risk of capacity for data center load to existing Ohio consumers.
filing-20260821-5281.quote: It will unreasonably shift the risks and costs associated with acquiring that new capacity from the data center loads to existing consumers in Ohio and elsewhere in PJM.

filing-20260821-5281.point: OCC objects that PJM relies on state allocation, and Ohio has no statute governing large-load capacity cost allocation.
filing-20260821-5281.quote: Ohio has no statutes governing allocation of large load-related generation capacity costs among retail customers.

filing-20260821-5281.point: OCC says nothing constrains suppliers from bidding the $555/MW-day cap, set against a 6,800 MW scarcity.
filing-20260821-5281.quote: The $555/MW-day (unforced capacity) offer cap is based on scarcity conditions and is significantly higher than the clearing price in the 2028/2029 auction of $325/MW-day

filing-20260821-5281.point: OCC notes the IMM calculated data center demand raised other customers' capacity costs by about $23.1 billion over three auctions.
filing-20260821-5281.quote: data center demand increased capacity costs to other PJM customers by approximately $23.1 billion across the 2025/2026, 2026/2027, 2027/2028 Base Residual Auctions.

filing-20260821-5281.point: OCC calls the 20 percent supplier shortage penalty too low and objects to passing penalties to load.
filing-20260821-5281.quote: PJM's proposal to limit the shortage penalty to 20% of the offer price for the capacity is also unjust, unreasonable and unduly discriminatory and preferential in favor of suppliers.

filing-20260821-5281.point: OCC backs the IMM approach of 15-year bilateral contracts for data center load with all risks on the counterparties.
filing-20260821-5281.quote: the IMM proposes that LSEs serving the new AI and large data center loads enter into 15-year bilateral contracts in which the risks and costs of the new generation to be acquired to serve those loads are allocated only to the parties to those contracts.

filing-20260821-5281.point: Alternatively OCC wants acceptance subject to refund and settlement or hearing built on the IMM proposal.
filing-20260821-5281.quote: if FERC accepts the filing, it should do so subject to refund and set the filing for hearing and/or settlement proceedings with directives that the parties use the IMM RBP proposal as a starting point.

filing-20260821-5096.point: OPSI supports the filing and asks FERC to act fast so later capacity auctions keep their schedule.
filing-20260821-5096.quote: OPSI encourages the Commission to act expeditiously so that PJM can implement the RBP without disrupting the schedule for subsequent capacity auctions.

filing-20260821-5096.point: OPSI backs a supplemental procurement equal to the 2028/2029 auction shortfall.
filing-20260821-5096.quote: OPSI supports PJM's proposal to implement a supplemental procurement of new capacity equal to the shortfall observed in the BRA for the 2028/2029 Delivery Year to serve large loads.

filing-20260821-5096.point: OPSI says allocating backstop costs to retail customers remains with state regulators.
filing-20260821-5096.quote: Under the Federal Power Act, the allocation of RBP costs to retail customers remains within the jurisdiction of retail regulators.

filing-20260821-5096.point: OPSI supports the new-capacity eligibility test so offsets add capacity.
filing-20260821-5096.quote: helps ensure that bilateral offsets and RBP procurements result in a genuine increase in regional capacity

filing-20260821-5096.point: OPSI strongly supports the voluntary bilateral matching process that lets large loads procure capacity and lower the procurement target.
filing-20260821-5096.quote: OPSI strongly supports the ongoing voluntary, iterative bilateral matching process through which new large loads may procure new capacity directly

filing-20260821-5096.point: OPSI recommends PJM revise the target and load forecast if load drops out before the procurement ends.
filing-20260821-5096.quote: should an electric distribution company ("EDC") / load serving entity ("LSE") confirm before completion of the RBP that a specific amount of load in the relevant load forecast is no longer expected to materialize, PJM would revise its RBP target and load forecast.

filing-20260821-5217.point: Pennsylvania OCA says PJM's filing creates a one-time procurement of new capacity driven mainly by data center load.
filing-20260821-5217.quote: a one-time procurement of new capacity to address resource adequacy challenges in the PJM Region arising from insufficient commitments of capacity in the 2027/2028 and 2028/2029 Reliability Pricing Model (RPM) Auctions

filing-20260821-5217.point: FERC, not the states, has jurisdiction over the methods that set peak load contribution values used to allocate capacity costs.
filing-20260821-5217.quote: FERC possesses—and states lack—jurisdiction to determine or approve the methods that are used to develop peak load contribution (PLC) and network service

filing-20260821-5217.point: PJM's plan to let states set backstop obligation values is called unjust and unreasonable because states would need jurisdiction they lack.
filing-20260821-5217.quote: PJM’s proposal is unjust and unreasonable because for states to determine the RBO values, they would have to determine and approve methods for RBO PLCs—and the states lack jurisdiction to do so.

filing-20260821-5217.point: If no state method is reported, PJM's fallback is pro rata allocation, which OCA says would charge non-large-load customers.
filing-20260821-5217.quote: pro rata RBP cost allocation to LSEs using PLC values is unjust and unreasonable because it will likely result in non-large load customers being allocated RBP costs, despite these ratepayers not having caused the costs.

filing-20260821-5217.point: OCA lays out three relief options and recommends the first: FERC exercises jurisdiction and orders mandatory Attachment M-2 filings.
filing-20260821-5217.quote: FERC should grant the first relief option by finding that PJM’s RBO cost allocation proposal is unjust and unreasonable, exercising jurisdiction over how RBO costs are allocated to LSEs, and directing all transmission owners to make mandatory Attachment M-2 filings

filing-20260821-5176.point: The Coalition says PJM's backstop filing lacks tools to align wholesale charges with state retail cost allocation.
filing-20260821-5176.quote: PJM’s filing lacks the tools needed to ensure that retail costs are, and will be, allocated in a just and reasonable manner at the state level.

filing-20260821-5176.point: Gap 1: wholesale costs must be designed with retail allocation in mind, tied to cost causation.
filing-20260821-5176.quote: Wholesale costs must be designed with retail allocation in mind; otherwise, simply claiming that states can allocate costs to retail customers may prove inadequate.

filing-20260821-5176.point: Gap 2: utilities' retail allocation methodologies should be on file with FERC or a state commission.
filing-20260821-5176.quote: While not mandating retail pricing, the FERC should require that methodologies be on file with the FERC or a relevant state commission.

filing-20260821-5176.point: Gap 3: PJM should add a separate billing line item for backstop costs, broken out by the load growth that caused them.
filing-20260821-5176.quote: PJM should create a new billing line item (similar to how PJM separately reports Transmission Enhancement, Generation Deactivation, or other itemized costs) tagged specifically as “Reliability Backstop Procurement” costs

filing-20260821-5176.point: PJM should add subaccounts identifying each large load by interconnection point and issue billing guidance.
filing-20260821-5176.quote: Under each billing line item related to RBP, PJM should add subaccounts identifying each individual large load customer by interconnection point.

filing-20260821-5145.point: West Virginia does not support the filing in its current form and timetable, citing weak support for the backstop target.
filing-20260821-5145.quote: The PSCWV does not support the filing in its present form and timetable because the proposal fails to provide adequate support that the target level of so-called backstop capacity is needed

filing-20260821-5145.point: PJM sets the initial target at the 6,831 MW shortfall seen in the July 2026 auction rather than waiting on bilateral matching.
filing-20260821-5145.quote: PJM is proposing the RBP based on a perceived 6,831 MW shortfall from its capacity target set for its last capacity auction.

filing-20260821-5145.point: At the $555 per MW-day cap the 15-year commitment could average $1.4 billion per year.
filing-20260821-5145.quote: could exceed an average of $1.4 billion per year.

filing-20260821-5145.point: Bilateral contracts let new large loads bear the cost of the capacity they need, shrinking the backstop target.
filing-20260821-5145.quote: Bilateral contracts allow the costs of new capacity to be assumed directly by the contracting new large loads, creating the need for that capacity.

filing-20260821-5145.point: West Virginia asks for two model runs, one with no new large load, to size any backstop need.
filing-20260821-5145.quote: FERC should require PJM to determine a new target for the RBP based on the model from its last capacity auction run under two different scenarios.

filing-20260821-5180.point: The protesters support PJM's one-time procurement sized to the 2028/2029 shortfall with costs allocated to zones and LSEs serving new large loads.
filing-20260821-5180.quote: PJM proposes a one-time procurement of new capacity sized to the 2028/2029 shortfall, with costs that will be allocated to the zones and load-serving entities (“LSEs”) serving the new large loads

filing-20260821-5180.point: They read four objectives into the RBP: right amount, new capacity, on time, and large loads bear their costs.
filing-20260821-5180.quote: Procure new capacity that is additive to the PJM system, not a mere reshuffling of existing resources;

filing-20260821-5180.point: PJM's RBP has no location requirement, which the protesters say makes success depend on large, slow and costly network upgrades.
filing-20260821-5180.quote: PJM’s proposal to allow RBP supply to be located anywhere in the footprint will make the RBP’s success reliant on large-scale network upgrades that will likely cause significant delays and incur significant costs.

filing-20260821-5180.point: The protesters cite PJM's forecast of 30 GW of large load by 2030 and 70 GW by 2038, and auction shortfalls of 6.8 GW and 6.5 GW.
filing-20260821-5180.quote: PJM predicts that 30 GW of large load demand will come online by 2030 and 70 GW of large load demand will come online by 2038.

filing-20260821-5180.point: The last three base residual auctions cleared at the price cap, up from $28.92/MW-day in 2024/2025.
filing-20260821-5180.quote: The past three BRAs cleared at the price cap, clearing at $325/MW-day in the 2028/2029 BRA, $333.44/MW-day in the 2027/2028 BRA, and $329.17/MW-day in the 2026/2027 BRA.

filing-20260821-5180.point: The primary fix is a locational requirement; paying 100% of network upgrades is a partial alternative that should be additional.
filing-20260821-5180.quote: the Commission view this modification as additional to a requirement that RBP supply be located near large loads, not as a completely sufficient alternative modification.

filing-20260821-5180.point: In PJM's Reliability Resource Initiative, 10 of 51 projects withdrew after upgrade costs were assigned, which the protesters offer as a warning.
filing-20260821-5180.quote: 10 out of 51 RRI projects withdrew from the interconnection process, with two projects dropping out before being studied, and eight projects dropping at the first decision point in TC2.

filing-20260821-5180.point: They liken state-mandated take-or-pay contracts between LSEs and large loads to the cost recovery agreement in the June 18 order.
filing-20260821-5180.quote: Take-or-pay contracts with respect to the RBP would work similarly to the cost-recovery agreements outlined in the Commission’s Order and would serve a similar purpose.

filing-20260819-5134.point: ICC generally supports PJM's one-time supplemental capacity procurement for large-load shortfalls.
filing-20260819-5134.quote: The ICC generally supports PJM's proposal to implement a one-time, supplemental procurement of new capacity to address the identified resource adequacy shortfall

filing-20260819-5134.point: ICC praises the bilateral phase because it assigns costs to the new load that contributed to the shortfall.
filing-20260819-5134.quote: Bilateral contracts provide new load with an opportunity to purchase capacity and address the shortfall to which they directly contributed.

filing-20260819-5134.point: ICC says the proposal has no mechanism to moderate load forecast error, and 15-year contracts could compound it.
filing-20260819-5134.quote: The PJM proposal does not include any mechanism to moderate any potential error, such as cost reconciliation.

filing-20260819-5134.point: ICC questions how retail access states can assign wholesale capacity costs to retail load through the new RBP Obligation.
filing-20260819-5134.quote: it is unclear how states, particularly retail access states like Illinois, would be able to assign wholesale capacity costs to retail load in the manner PJM proposes

filing-20260819-5134.point: ICC doubts that states are best placed to identify cost causers, which the E-7 order expects cost transparency to enable.
filing-20260819-5134.quote: expecting the states to make such determinations for PJM and the Commission may be unreasonable.

filing-20260819-5134.point: ICC asks that registry data reach all states and that PJM's non-disclosure form be flexible.
filing-20260819-5134.quote: the ICC, for instance, would not be in a position to sign the pro forma non-disclosure agreements to access confidential data from PJM as it reads at this time.

filing-20260814-5244.point: PJM says the June 30 example did not show least-cost selection by Delivery Year, so it submits corrected examples.
filing-20260814-5244.quote: the example provided in Exhibit 1 of Mrs. Croop’s June 30, 2026 affidavit did not accurately demonstrate the least cost selection by Delivery Year

filing-20260814-5244.point: PJM argues the supplement changes no rate, term or condition and so is not an amendment.
filing-20260814-5244.quote: the supplemental affidavit merely updates the examples, also shown in redline, that were included in Mrs. Croop’s June 30, 2026 affidavit and does not revise or amend a proposed rate schedule, term, or condition.

filing-20260814-5244.point: PJM asks FERC to keep the September 29, 2026 action date.
filing-20260814-5244.quote: the Commission should continue to issue an order by the requested action date of September 29, 2026.

filing-20260814-5244.point: The affidavit corrects an inverted numerator and denominator in the MW-weighted average levelized cost explanation.
filing-20260814-5244.quote: incorrectly inverted the numerator and denominator

filing-20260814-5244.point: Offers are levelized at a 9.5% after-tax WACC and selected under a maximum willingness to pay, illustrated at $100/MW-day against the proposed $555/MW-day.
filing-20260814-5244.quote: rather than a maximum willingness to pay of $555/MW-day as PJM is proposing to use for the RBP, we assume that the maximum willingness to pay is $100/MW-day

filing-20260814-5244.point: In Example 3 the procurement clears 100 MW short of the 6,800 MW target to stay under the price cap.
filing-20260814-5244.quote: the procurement would clear 100 MW short the target, with the maximum UCAP MW procured equal to 6,700 MW for the 2031/32 Delivery Year.

filing-er26-3380-pjm-original.point: PJM describes the RBP as a one-time procurement responding to capacity shortfalls driven by large loads, mainly data centers.
filing-er26-3380-pjm-original.quote: a one-time procurement of new capacity to address resource adequacy challenges in the PJM Region

filing-er26-3380-pjm-original.point: PJM ties the RBP to the NEDC/PJM Governors' Principles: a backstop auction, 15-year price certainty, and cost allocation to LSEs with new data centers that have not self-procured.
filing-er26-3380-pjm-original.quote: allocate the cost of any new capacity procured through the aforementioned [RBP] to [Load Serving Entities ("LSE")] with new data centers that have not self-procured new capacity or agreed to be curtailable.

filing-er26-3380-pjm-original.point: PJM cites a forecast of 32 GW of peak growth from 2024 to 2030, 30 GW from data centers.
filing-er26-3380-pjm-original.quote: PJM's load forecast predicts peak load growth of 32 gigawatts [("GW")] from 2024 to 2030, 30 GW of which is projected to be from data centers.

filing-er26-3380-pjm-original.point: The 2028/2029 auction cleared 6,831.3 MW short of the reliability requirement at the $325/MW-day price cap.
filing-er26-3380-pjm-original.quote: cleared 6,831.3 MW (in Unforced Capacity ("UCAP")) short of PJM's Regional Transmission Organization ("RTO")-wide reliability requirement at the market price cap of $325/MW-day.

filing-er26-3380-pjm-original.point: RBP Resources get commitments of up to 15 years, from 2028/2029 through 2042/2043.
filing-er26-3380-pjm-original.quote: for a fixed term of up to 15 years, starting with the 2028/2029 Delivery Year and ending with the 2042/2043 Delivery Year.

filing-er26-3380-pjm-original.point: PJM caps the MW-weighted levelized procurement cost at $555/MW-day.
filing-er26-3380-pjm-original.quote: not exceed a maximum willingness to pay of $555/MW-day UCAP, on a MW-weighted average basis over all Delivery Years of the RBP.

filing-er26-3380-pjm-original.point: PJM selects resources pay-as-bid rather than at a single clearing price, because the RBP is one-time and procures non-uniform resources.
filing-er26-3380-pjm-original.quote: PJM proposes to commit resources in the RBP using a pay-as-bid approach,

filing-er26-3380-pjm-original.point: Costs go to Electric Distributor zones, then to LSEs, using state or RERRA allocations when reported, with a PJM back-up method.
filing-er26-3380-pjm-original.quote: the proposed cost allocation methodology empowers states and/or RERRAs to submit RBP RBOs, which PJM would then apply to the allocation of RBP Charges to LSEs.

filing-er26-3380-pjm-original.point: PJM asks for an order by September 29 and plans to open the window September 30, 2026, and consents to modification or severance.
filing-er26-3380-pjm-original.quote: PJM requests that the Commission issue an order on this filing and make this proposal effective by no later than September 29, 2026, which is 60 days after the date of this filing.
